core_obligations: Follow the proof of the proper base change theorem to reduce the statement to the identity of the stalk of the pushforward at a point with the sections over the fibre (proof lines 3157-3159).
Follow the proof of the topological proper base change lemma to reduce that identity to the zeroth degree case of the closed-subset lemma (proof lines 3160-3161).
Note that the first part of the proof of that lemma works for sheaves of sets, which gives the result (proof lines 3162-3163).

Observe the argument is insensitive to the group structure (proof lines 3162-3163).
difficulty_reason: In a cartesian square of topological spaces with the vertical map f proper, the lemma shows that the inverse image of the pushforward of a sheaf of sets equals the pushforward of the inverse image along the base change (statement lines 3142-3154). The proof is a reduction of the whole argument of the proper base change theorem to the case of sheaves of sets: it suffices to identify the stalk of the pushforward at a point with the sections over the fibre, and that identification is reduced to the zeroth degree case of the closed-subset cohomology lemma, whose first part works verbatim for sheaves of sets (proof lines 3156-3164). The claim is H2: the same reduction as the abelian case, with the recognition that the only input used is insensitive to the absence of a group structure, and the omitted details are bounded.
